policy: One identity per distinct writing. Canonical grouping is not fixed by a modern book count. Multiple manuscripts and translations link to the same writing where identity is established; distinct compositions and retellings remain separate. The WLC source-edition field is populated only for writings actually supplied in OSHB v2.2. It is a later comparison witness and is never used to infer that an earlier DSS, Samaritan, or other manuscript survives for a passage.

records.title: Sirach (Ben Sira)
records.description: A distinct writing preserved in fragmentary Hebrew witnesses and ancient translations. Surviving Hebrew manuscript text, Greek and Syriac witnesses, and later editorial Hebrew restorations are kept as separate textual layers.

source_editions.source_name: Swete Septuagint — Greek Sirach
source_editions.source_status: Greek edition source included; not a diplomatic transcription of one codex
source_editions.witness_basis: Greek Septuagint textual tradition as represented by the Swete edition
source_editions.transcription_type: edited Greek text; retained as a separate versional witness

source_editions.source_name: David Kahana, Ben Sira (1912), Hebrew edition
source_editions.source_status: source importer added; text extraction and passage-level verification required
source_editions.witness_basis: Kahana's edition based chiefly on Cairo Genizah Hebrew manuscripts; square-bracketed passages in the Wikisource transcription identify Hebrew retroversions where the Hebrew source was absent
source_editions.transcription_type: early printed Hebrew edition with manuscript-based readings and explicitly marked editorial Hebrew retroversions; not a diplomatic transcription of one manuscript
source_editions.license: 1912 printed edition public domain; Wikisource transcription CC BY-SA 4.0

records.reconstruction_policy: For each passage, prefer surviving Hebrew manuscript readings (Qumran, Masada, and Cairo Genizah) with exact manuscript and fragment coordinates. Where Hebrew is absent, compare the oldest available Greek and Syriac witnesses for the same passage. Any Hebrew retroversion must remain labelled as an editorial reconstruction, never as an ancient Hebrew manuscript reading. Preserve lacunae when no reliable witness supplies the wording.
